sentences.text: Macgowania was a small ichthyosaur, a marine reptile, with a total body length of approximately 3 meters.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a partial skeleton (ROM 41992) that preserves a nearly complete skull, an almost complete forefin, and other postcranial elements.
The specific name janiceps is derived from Janus, the Roman god with two faces, and ceps, meaning 'with a head'.
A second specimen was preserved in a fractured rock slab on a steep slope above the Graham River, facing immediate destruction.
This second specimen was discovered by a British Columbian outdoor club in August 2009 and later identified as Macgowania janiceps by Donald Henderson in 2015.
Macgowania was originally described by Chris McGowan in 1996 under the name Ichthyosaurus janiceps.
Ryosuke Motani reassigned the species to its own genus in 1999, establishing Macgowania janiceps as the type species.
Macgowania belongs to the order Ichthyosauria.
Macgowania is classified within the unranked group Parvipelvia.
The family Macgowaniidae was named by McGowan and Motani in 2003 to include the genus Macgowania.
Macgowania fossils date to the middle Norian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 210 million years ago.
The time range for Macgowania is the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
